declared_before_compute.functional: eps(n, y) = F_F(n, M_N y) + U(y) + C_v n^2/(2 y^2) (symmetric matter, g = 4); beta matter, isovector C(n) = C0 (n/n0)^gamma with C0 = 8 (J - T)/n0, gamma from L, exactly as closure/nvg_forward_band.py (power form, consistent pressure)
declared_before_compute.normalisation: every 1-parameter form is written U = theta f(y) with f(1) = f'(1) = 0, f''(1) = 1, so theta = U_yy(1) [MeV^4] and the vacuum scalar mass is m_s = sqrt(theta)/W0 (m_s^2 = d^2U/dW^2 at W0)

B1_anomaly_d1.U: B0 W0^4 [y^4 (ln y - 1/4) + 1/4] = theta f_4(y),  f_a(y) = y^a ln y / a - (y^a - 1)/a^2,  theta = 4 B0 W0^4
B1_anomaly_d1.derivation: Scale (dilatation) Ward identity: if the ONLY breaking of scale invariance is the trace anomaly carried by a dimension-4 operator built from W (theta^mu_mu = 4U - W U_W = const - kappa W^4), the general solution is U = A W^4 ln W + C W^4 + D.  Vacuum at W0 (U_W(W0) = 0) and zero vacuum energy (U(W0) = 0) fix C and D, leaving U = A [W^4 (ln(W/W0) - 1/4) + W0^4/4], A = B0 (Schechter 1980 PRD 21 3393; Heide-Rudaz-Ellis 1994 NPA 571 713 for the nuclear-matter use).  U(1) invariant (function of |Phi| only).  Bounded below on W >= 0, single minimum at W0, U(0) = B0 W0^4/4 = |eps_vac|.  Inflection at y = exp(-1/3) = 0.7165 (U_yy < 0 below).

zero_parameter_normalisations.GC: full trace anomaly carried by W: eps_vac = <theta^mu_mu>/4 = -(b/32) <(alpha_s/pi) G^2>, b = 11 - 2 N_f/3 = 9 (N_f = 3); U(0) = (9/32) <(alpha_s/pi) G^2>, central <(alpha_s/pi) G^2> = 0.012 GeV^4 (SVZ 1979); sensitivity x0.5 and x2 (0.006, 0.024 GeV^4)
zero_parameter_normalisations.m_sigma_action: m_s = sqrt(2 lambda) W0 with the action's lambda = 1.05: m_s = 1244.8 MeV
zero_parameter_normalisations.f0_500: m_s = 450 MeV (f0(500) pole region, PDG 400-550 MeV, from memory; the synthesis's discrete hypothesis)
zero_parameter_normalisations.glueball_0pp: m_s = 1700 MeV (lightest 0++ glueball, quenched lattice about 1.65-1.75 GeV, from memory)
zero_parameter_normalisations.rule: theta fixed => only C_v free => impose P(n0) = 0 at n0 in {0.15, 0.16, 0.17}; E/A, y*, K predicted; a member exists only if the predicted E/A lies in [-16.5, -15.5] MeV (otherwise: 'does not saturate in the window', adverse)

B2_anomaly_d.derivation: Same Ward identity when W is not itself the dilaton chi but scales like chi^d (W/W0 = (chi/chi0)^d): substituting into the d = 1 solution gives the Furnstahl-Serot-Tang 1995 type logarithmic potential (S/S0)^(4/d) [(1/(2d)) ln(S^2/S0^2) - 1/4] (form recalled from memory, rederived here).  theta^mu_mu = 4U - d W U_W = (d^2/4) theta (1 - y^a): the anomaly is proportional to y^a = (chi/chi0)^4, so the gluon-condensate normalisation is U(0) = theta/a^2 = |eps_vac| for every d.

discrete_choices.d2: a = 2: W^2 carries scale dimension 2 relative to chi (the FST-type choice d about 2; attribution from memory, unverified)
discrete_choices.d3: a = 4/3: W proportional to the quark condensate q-bar q (dimension 3), the order parameter of the linear sigma model
discrete_choices.d4: a = 1: W proportional to the gluon operator G^2 (dimension 4): Schechter's H ln(H/Lambda^4) with H = W

B3_coleman_weinberg.U: lambda W0^4 (y^2-1)^2/4 + eps_VF(y) [Chin 1977 nucleon sea, gamma = 4] + V_vec(y) [3 (q_phi W)^4 ...] + lambda^2 [V_sigma(y) + V_G(y)] renormalised in scheme T4 (Taylor through 4th order at W0 subtracted from every loop) or S3 (U(1)-symmetric counterterms 1, W^2, W^4 for the bosons), Goldstone 'drop' or 'ms'; reused from missing/vacuum/vacuum_oneloop.py (sea_y, BosonLoops)
B3_coleman_weinberg.derivation: the action's own one-loop effective potential (Landau gauge, MS-bar) with the tree quartic lambda the only parameter.  With mu^2 = 2 lambda W0^2 the sigma and Goldstone loops are exactly lambda^2 times lambda-independent functions and the nucleon and vector loops are lambda independent; schemes remove all mu dependence (checked in vacuum_oneloop.self_test)
B3_coleman_weinberg.zero_parameter: the action's lambda = 1.05 (only C_v free): P(n0) = 0 at n0 in {0.15, 0.16, 0.17}, E/A predicted

B4a_U1_quartic.U: lambda W0^4 (y^2-1)^2/4 = theta f_{2,4}(y), theta = 2 lambda W0^4
B4a_U1_quartic.derivation: most general renormalisable U(1)-invariant potential (|Phi|^2, |Phi|^4) with vacuum at W0: the action's own tree form with lambda freed (B3 without loops)

B4b_harmonic_W.derivation: U(1)-invariant (function of |Phi| only) but non-analytic in |Phi|^2: explicit scale breaking by a dimension-1 and a dimension-2 operator, i.e. the linear-sigma (Walecka) form with sigma = W0 - W

B4_symmetry_forms.two_power_family_note: B4a, B4b, B1 and B2 are all members of f_{p,q}(y) = [p y^q - q y^p + (q - p)]/(p q (q - p)) (scale breaking by operators of dimensions p and q; the log forms are the p = q limits); no other (p, q) has a derivation from the listed symmetries and none is added

B4c_anomaly_plus_U1_quartic.derivation: most general potential with a W^4 ln W anomaly plus the renormalisable U(1) operators (W^4, W^2, 1), vacuum at W0 with zero energy: A W^4 ln(W/W0) + c4 W^4 + c2 W^2 + c0 with two constraints = 2 free parameters
B4c_anomaly_plus_U1_quartic.constraint: theta1 >= 0 (otherwise unbounded below at large y); the (V) check decides the rest

solver.one_parameter_linear: U_t(y) = P_F + n0 V/2, U'_t(y) = (n0 V - M y n_s)/y, V = M + E/A - E_F*(y) (same algebra as scalar_jet); root of U_t f' - U'_t f = 0 in y in [0.30, 0.995] (all sign changes on a 1400-point grid, brentq); theta = U'_t/f'
solver.CW: at each y solve lambda from stationarity (quadratic in lambda), root of the energy residual in y
solver.two_parameter: theta from (U, U') linear solve, root of U'' - U''_t(K) in y
solver.zero_parameter: theta fixed; root in y of P_F - U + (M n_s + U') y/2 = 0 at n0 (P = 0 with stationarity); C_v = (M n_s + U') y^3/n0^2
solver.admissibility_of_a_root: C_v > 0, theta > 0, d2eps/dy2 > 0 at (n0, y*), K > 0, and y* the global minimum of eps(n0, y) over y in [0.02, 1.5]

declared_before_compute.class_sample: per admissible form: LHS of N = 40 points over (n0, E/A, J, L) [+ K for B4c] uniform on the windows, seed 20261113; if total compute would exceed the budget, N is reduced to 24 for every form alike (decided before seeing any stellar number)

structural_K_algebra.statement: K = 240 MeV at y* = 0.60 / 0.65 / 0.70 requires U_yy/U_y = 6.8 / 4.0 / 1.9 at y* (U_y < 0, i.e. a strongly concave potential); the derived bases give f''/f' = 1.74 / 1.04 / 0.28 (log4, the largest) and <= -0.2 for all others at the same y*.

validation.exact_dirac_check: quartic y* = 0.87: exact Dirac 1.054367 MeV reproduces creative/spin_orbit variants exact_dirac (1.054367)
validation.note: the quartic at y* = 0.87 has a second local minimum at y = 1.377 (U > 0): globally stable (old rule q >= 0) but it fails this direction's stricter single-minimum (V); its 8-term chi2 at J = 32, L = 50 is 30.82

free_parameters_added.statement: No parameter is added to the action.  The polynomial scalar sector of the forward chain (a2, a3, a4 [, a5] plus a chosen y*) is replaced by derived one-parameter forms: per member 2 continuous scalar-sector parameters (theta or lambda, C_v), both fixed by P(n0) = 0 and E/A, i.e. 2 fewer than the quartic chain; the zero-parameter normalisations leave only C_v; B4c has 3 (theta1, theta2, C_v) fixed by P = 0, E/A, K.  Discrete choices: 6 one-parameter shapes + 4 CW renormalisation variants + 1 two-parameter form + 13 zero-parameter normalisations, all enumerated before computing, none chosen by data.  Isovector (J, L) as in the chain.

key_results: VALIDATION: the solvers return the inverse-jet quartic exactly (y* 0.87, E/A -16, K 240, Q0 -417.49 to 1e-12; theta = 1 to 1e-14), and the generalised chain reproduces the native chain bit for bit (max relative difference 0.0 over M_max, radii, Lambda, rotation shifts, S_2, E_PNM, K_sym, chi2 30.82) and 16O 1p = 1.0396 MeV.

PREDICTIONS (n0, E/A over the full windows): B1 W^4 ln W: m*/M 0.703-0.712, K 1525-1648 MeV; B2 d=2: 0.815-0.822, K 447-480; d=3: 0.832-0.839, K 375-400; d=4 (Schechter H ln H): 0.840-0.846, K 350-372; B4a U(1) quartic: 0.777-0.785, K 664-720; B4b harmonic: 0.829-0.835, K 390-416; B3 Coleman-Weinberg T4: 0.789-0.797, K 627-676 (lambda = 0.0055); S3: 0.672-0.681, K 2219-2365.  Exactly one root per grid point for every form.

KEY QUESTION: no derived form gives m*/M in [0.55, 0.70] with K in [220, 260].  The two forms that reach m*/M <= 0.712 (B1, CW-S3) predict K = 1525-2365 MeV; the lowest predicted K is 350 MeV (d = 4) at m*/M = 0.846.  B4c (the only form with K as input) needs a negative anomaly coefficient for K in [220, 260] and is unbounded below there; a bounded B4c needs K >= 692 MeV.

WHY: B = d mu/dy = M^2 y/E_F* - 2 C_v n0/y^3 vanishes at y* = 0.634 because the vector mass scales with W; near and below that point K -> 9 n0 D = 2600-3000 MeV unless the scalar curvature cancels.  K = 240 at y* = 0.60-0.65 needs U_yy/U_y = 6.8-4.0 (strongly concave at saturation); derived shapes give at most 1.7-1.0 (log4).

VACUUM SCALAR MASS: every saturating admissible form predicts m_s = sqrt(U_yy(1))/W0 = 86-101 MeV (79-87 for the inadmissible B4c) (the same light scalar as the polynomial chain, 79-84 MeV).  Hence every zero-parameter normalisation with a heavy scalar fails to bind: action lambda = 1.05 (m_s 1245), f0(500) 450, glueball 1700, full gluon condensate with d = 1 (270 MeV): P(n0) = 0 at y* 0.95-0.9995 with E/A = +7.2 ... +8.2 MeV (no saturation, K < 0).

ZERO-PARAMETER HIT: the trace-anomaly form with d = 3 (W ~ q-bar q) and the full SVZ condensate (0.012 GeV^4) is the only normalisation with a member in the E/A window (n0 in [0.165, 0.170], E/A predicted -15.5 ... -16.49 MeV; m_s 90.2 MeV): m*/M 0.833-0.836, K 381-400 MeV (adverse vs [220, 260]), 16O 1p 1.50 MeV, class PPC 0.028, LOO z J0614 -2.49.  It is 1 of 4 d-values at the declared central condensate (x0.5 and x2 shift E/A by tens of MeV).

STARS (S): best classes are d = 3, d = 4, harmonic, d=3-GC: PPC 0.023-0.028 (< 0.05), LOO max |z| 2.49-2.74, all from the J0614 radius (R(1.44) static 12.3-13.6 km); without J0614 (sensitivity only) PPC 0.12-0.15, max |z| 1.47-1.80.  ln Z = -10.1 ... -10.25 for d = 3, d = 4, harmonic (d=3-GC: -9.75 over its member n0 range, -11.15 over the full n0 window), vs -14.24 for the declared polynomial class and lnL(DD-ME2) = -9.98.  Lower-m* forms are far worse: B1 PPC 0 (best chi2 71.7, R(1.44) 13.9-14.8 km, Lambda_1.4 ~1240), CW-S3 PPC 0 (best chi2 146, E_PNM(0.10) = 22 MeV).  2-sigma box: 0 of 358 propagated members (2 CW-S3 members have no eps-continuous SLy match and get L = 0).

SPIN-ORBIT (O): 16O 1p = 1.36-1.95 MeV for every form with m*/M >= 0.815; 2.2-2.7 MeV for B4a and CW-T4; 4.05-4.45 MeV (exact Dirac 4.16-4.79) for B1 at m*/M 0.71 (fails, just below 4.9); 5.53-5.88 MeV (exact Dirac 5.80-6.60) for CW-S3 at m*/M 0.68 (passes, but WS-fit rms 6.6 MeV and (V) fails).

GROUND STATE (G): holds for every propagated member (358 of 358 with a computed nuclear block and crust match); no Lee-Wick state below E/A(n0) - 0.05 MeV up to the M_max centre; the design branch reaches y -> 1 at n -> 0 and is the ground state on 0-0.20 fm^-3 for every form.

VACUUM (V): holds for all six one-parameter derived shapes (single minimum at W0, U >= 0); fails for every Coleman-Weinberg member (the nucleon loop wins at large W: U(10 W0) = -5e13 ... -9e13 MeV^4 because the fitted lambda = 0.0055-0.0067, 160-190 times below the action's 1.05, is far below the boson-loop stabilisation threshold) and for B4c with K in the window.

JOINT: no form converges.  The (O)-(S) anticorrelation of the polynomial class persists with derived potentials: the only forms with 16O 1p near or inside the window (m*/M 0.68-0.71) predict K = 1.5-2.4 GeV and stars with R(1.44) >= 13.9 km (PPC 0); forms whose stars are marginal (m*/M 0.83-0.85) give 16O 1p = 1.4-1.7 MeV.

verdict_text: Derived non-polynomial potentials make m*/M and K genuine predictions, and the predictions are adverse.  Over the full (n0, E/A) windows the six one-parameter shapes derived from the scale Ward identity (W^4 ln W, its d = 2, 3, 4 variants, the U(1) quartic, the harmonic form) and the action's own Coleman-Weinberg potential predict m*/M = 0.67-0.85 with K = 350-2365 MeV; none reaches m*/M 0.55-0.70 with K in [220, 260], and the two-parameter anomaly + U(1) form reaches K in the window only with a negative anomaly coefficient (unbounded below).  The structural reason is the W-dependent vector mass: B = d mu/dy vanishes at y* = 0.634, so low m* forces K -> 2.6-3.0 GeV unless the potential is tuned to be strongly concave at saturation, which no derived shape is.  Every saturating form needs a light vacuum scalar (86-101 MeV), so normalisations by the action's lambda, f0(500), the glueball or the d = 1 gluon condensate do not bind.  Through the joint test: (S) fails for every class (best PPC 0.028 with LOO z(J0614) = -2.49 for the zero-parameter d = 3 condensate form; 0.023-0.026 for d = 3, d = 4, harmonic), (O) fails for every form with a bounded potential (1.4-4.4 MeV), (O) passes only for the Coleman-Weinberg S3 member (5.5-5.9 MeV) whose potential is unbounded below (V fails), whose K is 2.3 GeV and whose stars give chi2 >= 146; (G) holds everywhere.  Verdict: does_not_converge.
practical_value: A zero-free-scalar-coefficient NVG EOS family: the trace-anomaly potentials theta f_a(y) with theta fixed by E/A give the equation of state, M_max, radii and Lambda from (n0, E/A, J, L) alone (e.g. d = 4 central member: m*/M 0.843, K 361, M_max 2.005, R(1.44) 12.79 km, Lambda_1.4 577, chi2 18.2); usable as a falsifiable baseline that is better in evidence (ln Z -10.1 ... -10.3) than the polynomial class (-14.2).

A diagnostic rule for any model with a W-scaled vector mass: K = 9 n0 (D - B^2/C) with B -> 0 at m*/M = 0.634, so asking for m*/M ~ 0.6 and K ~ 240 is a fine-tuning demand on U_yy (table in derivation.structural_K_algebra); an RMF-like spin-orbit cannot come from the scalar potential alone in this action.

The predicted vacuum scalar mass 86-101 MeV is shape independent: any proposal that identifies the NVG scalar with f0(500), the glueball or the action's 1245 MeV sigma is excluded by saturation, not only by surfaces.

dpot.py: drop-in generalisation of the validated chain to any callable U(y) (bit-identical on the polynomial case), with saturation solvers for 0, 1 and 2 parameter forms, a vacuum check, a Lee-Wick scan and the 16O 1p LDA.
caveats: Class samples are N = 40 LHS points per form (4-dimensional prior; the d=3-GC class samples only its member range n0 in [0.165, 0.170], 24.7 % of the n0 window); ESS 1.8-14.8; 2 of 40 CW-S3 points fail the eps-continuous SLy match (L = 0).  PPC values of 0.02-0.03 are below 0.05 by less than the sampling error of the polynomial-class study (bootstrap spread there 0.037-0.057); the LOO J0614 failure (|z| 2.5-2.7) and the (O) failure are not near threshold.

Spin-orbit is the LDA first-order procedure validated on NL3 / DD-ME2 / FSUGold (6.84 / 6.51 / 5.76 MeV); for m*/M <= 0.71 the Woods-Saxon fit rms is 3.4-6.6 MeV (0.4 for NL3), so the B1 (4.05-4.45) and CW-S3 (5.5-5.9) numbers carry a protocol uncertainty of order 0.3-0.8 MeV (exact Dirac in the same potentials: 4.16-4.79 and 5.80-6.60).  This does not rescue B1 robustly (exact Dirac 4.79 at most) and does not affect the CW-S3 verdict (V and S fail).

The FST / HRE attributions of the d-family and the d about 2 value are from memory; the forms themselves are derived here from the scale Ward identity.  The gluon condensate (0.012 GeV^4), f0(500) (450 MeV) and glueball (1.7 GeV) values are from memory; the condensate x0.5 / x2 sensitivities move E/A by 10-40 MeV, so the d = 3 zero-parameter hit is normalisation-fragile.

Coleman-Weinberg: one loop, Landau gauge; away from stationary points the potential is gauge dependent; the Goldstone 'ms' variant has a log-divergent U_yy at W0; its fitted lambda is 0.0055-0.0067 (200 times below the action's 1.05), so the boson loops are negligible and the nucleon sea + vector loop dominate.

(V) as declared here (single minimum) is stricter than the old q >= 0 rule; the old-rule quartic at y* = 0.87 fails it (second minimum at y = 1.377).  No derived one-parameter shape is affected (each has a single minimum).
